title: Workspace and home persistence contract (preservation matrix)

sandbox_runtime.resource_id: independent resource ID (instance ID + generation) per usage-ledger #2; runtime.started/stopped events meter it, and its lifecycle is not derived from volume state

workspace_volume.resource_id: independent volume resource ID per usage-ledger #2; provisioned/resized/released events carry the full quantity vector; lifecycle NOT derived from sandbox observed_state

home_volume.resource_id: independent volume resource ID per usage-ledger #2, separate from the workspace volume; only approved (allowlisted) home data is persisted, never all of home

snapshot.resource_id: independent snapshot ID per usage-ledger #2; owned by snapshot.created/expired/deleted events with its own retention, independent of the sandbox runtime

events.trigger: POST /v1/sandboxes/{id}/state {state: Suspend, suspend_mode: cold}; observed Suspend only after Runner-confirmed process stop

details.sandbox_runtime: processes stopped; RAM, PIDs, sockets and the original tmux screen are not kept; runtime tmpfs credentials cleared (key re-sent by CLI on resume, else 409 credentials_required); the compute metering interval closes only at the confirmed stop (runtime.stopped), never at HTTP 202
details.workspace_volume: approved workspace volume retained; volume_provisioned storage metering keeps running while the volume exists
details.home_volume: approved home volume retained, including the recorded Claude session ID and cwd
details.snapshot: independent resource; suspend does not touch the snapshot lifecycle

guarded_by: #12 acceptance: after cold Suspend/Resume, container recreation and runner restart, marker, repo and required agent settings exist
#12 (2026-10-02 inventory): volume retention still meters usage (#77 cross-check)
lifecycle contract: Suspending->Suspend requires Runner-confirmed stop; credentials_required refusal keeps the sandbox in Suspend

events.trigger: resume from Suspend via Resuming: valid credentials, capacity admission (volume_bytes) and disk checks pass; new generation and fencing token allocated

details.sandbox_runtime: a NEW execution instance starts with a new generation; no RAM, processes, tmux/socket or rootfs writable layer carry-over; ephemeral credentials are not preserved, the CLI re-sends the key
details.workspace_volume: the same volume is re-attached; no re-clone and no overwrite of an existing repo (docs/contracts/work-image.md idempotent init)
details.home_volume: the same volume is re-attached; the session ID/cwd record survives; a missing record reports session_missing instead of silently loading another conversation

guarded_by: #12 acceptance: cold Suspend/Resume keeps marker, repo and required agent settings; secrets are never written into copyable work files
work-image contract: a non-empty workspace skips clone and is never overwritten (scripts/clone_args.py should_skip_clone)

events.trigger: DELETE /v1/sandboxes/{id} with explicit data-deletion scope confirmation and expected_version; Destroying -> Destroyed after one-by-one confirmed removal

details.sandbox_runtime: processes confirmed terminated; session secret injection revoked and cleared
details.workspace_volume: the first-version workspace volume is removed only after the explicit data-deletion scope confirmation; existing backups follow their own retention-based deletion flow
details.home_volume: the home volume and session index are deleted
details.snapshot: destroy does NOT imply snapshot deletion: snapshots are independent resources with their own created/expired/deleted events and retention; snapshot ledger rows stay alive until their own confirmed deletion

guarded_by: #12 acceptance: destroy/expiry recycling distinguishes compute deletion from data deletion; retention/trash rules are consistent with a human-confirmed data-deletion boundary
usage-ledger #2: sandbox destroy must not assume backups or snapshots are already deleted

events.trigger: memory_limit_terminated confirmed (container actually stopped, exit 137, OOMKilled=true, current generation); after reconcile, explicit restart -> Resuming -> Active with a new generation

details.sandbox_runtime: the old instance is gone: RAM, processes, tmux/socket, rootfs writable layer and ephemeral credentials are not preserved; a fresh execution instance is created with a new generation (recreation, not a same-container docker start); a bounded exec health check is required before Active
details.workspace_volume: the approved workspace volume is kept across stop/restart; volume identity is saved in control-plane metadata before launch; committed/fsynced files are preserved, application-buffer and partial-write loss is accepted
details.home_volume: the approved home volume is kept; the recorded session ID and cwd are preserved; session-ID reconnection stays unverified until paid E05/E10

guarded_by: #12 (2026-10-02 inventory): recreation must show recreation/session-ID evidence, not pass off a same-container docker start as recreation
#67 ADR: same approved volumes across stop/restart; credentials are protected separately from approved persisted data and never key-stashed in a volume
#11 runtime recreation and #17 operation/reconcile acceptance remain pending

events.trigger: volume quantity change passes admission (volume_bytes) and is confirmed; emitted as resource.resized with the full new quantity vector

details.workspace_volume: data preserved; only the provisioned quantity changes; resize follows the volume's own resource lifecycle and is not derived from sandbox observed_state
details.home_volume: same semantics as the workspace volume when resized

guarded_by: #12 acceptance: permissions and usage caps are verifiable (volume_bytes admission on create/resume)
usage-ledger #2: volume resize cannot be derived from sandbox state alone; policy.applied/resource.resized events carry the full quantity vector

events.trigger: snapshot TTL reached; expiry issues a delete request only; the confirmed deletion ends snapshot_stored metering

details.snapshot: TTL expiry issues a delete request only; metering ends on confirmed deletion; both the retention deadline and the actual release time are recorded

guarded_by: usage-ledger #2 + ledger-examples.json snapshot case: TTL 2s expiry with 3s confirmed deletion meters 6,144,000 byte*ms (deadline and release both recorded)

invariants.statement: workspace/home volumes and snapshots have independent resource IDs; provision/resize/release follow their own resource events and are never derived from sandbox observed_state (usage-ledger #2).
sandbox destroy removes the first-version workspace/home volumes but never assumes backup or snapshot deletion; snapshot rows stay alive until their own confirmed deletion.
snapshot TTL expiry records the retention deadline and only requests deletion; the actual release is recorded separately and ends storage metering on confirmed deletion, not on request acceptance.
cold suspend stops compute metering only at the Runner-confirmed stop; volume_provisioned and snapshot_stored meters keep running while the storage exists.
the API key lives in runtime tmpfs only and is cleared on stop; it never enters DB, log, image, volume or backup; resume without the key stays Suspend with 409 credentials_required.

cold_restart.no_reclone_no_overwrite: an existing non-empty workspace skips clone and is never overwritten; an empty workspace clones via argv-safe git clone -- <url> <dest>; contract: docs/contracts/work-image.md (scripts/clone_args.py)
cold_restart.session_id_stable: the recorded Claude session ID survives suspend/resume and execution-instance recreation; recreation evidence must show a new instance with a new generation, not a same-container docker start
cold_restart.cwd_preserved: the recorded working directory is preserved across cold restart; resume uses the explicit session/cwd record
cold_restart.missing_session_reported: a missing session record reports session_missing so the user chooses a new session; another conversation is never silently loaded
cold_restart.init_runs_once: first-boot initialization (fixed tmux session name, node-owned /workspace) runs exactly once across first boot, reboot and cold recovery (work-image idempotent contract)
